q: Rain falling down on me, I woke in the dark, choking, with Styx—'Grandpa'—absentmindedly patting my chest as if seawater wasn't spewing from my mouth.
“Easy, Maddox. You'll breathe right again soon.” He laughed as I shoved at his old face, forcing him away from me. He is not who I wanted to see.

It was all fucking real: the sparkling water, the call to the sea, the bike plunging into the ocean. And then her, there, saving me. Again. Just like she had that fateful day when I plunged into the Atlantic at age ten.

In a dreamlike surrender, I spread my arms wide, inviting the storm above and embracing the gratitude in my heart. “Sa-leen-i.” It felt so good to have an answer. Such relief to know I hadn't been crazy this whole time, believing in a magical childhood friend.

For so many agonizing years, through upheavals and relocations from the East Coast to the West, to California, through heart-wrenching losses, I had held on to a glimpse of hope that she was out there, remembering me as I did her.

It was as if she knew my dying was her death. Us being parted from each other, once more, would end her existence. I felt her fate tethered to mine, resonating inside me, which was insanely intense while drowning.

Where legs should've been, her skin was darker, inlaid with multiple colors. They matched her hair, which consisted of mystical blues and greens —no scales, as I had seen in so many cartoons and movies. Then, as her tail tapered in, I was finally able to see her one impressive fin.
Saleeni was under the rear of the bike, resting the back tire on her shoulder. Her eyes then glowed a magnificent green when her jaw locked and her whole tail started to propel us upward…

Not only did I have Tallulah, but I also had a whole little family of friends I wanted to reach out to. My fellow fosters—Sarah, Ethan, Gage, Sebastian, and Finn. I even wanted to hear from Dale and Harmony, our foster parents, just a quick clip of their voices.
There was no joking around about sex. Styx was telling me a dark secret I could feel closing in on me.
Noma had told me Dad's mom had died at birth, as mine did. The similarity seemed coincidental. That belief was so wrong.
Styx wiped under his eyes and his nose, then told me, “And handed me my son.”

Nothing inside me worried that Styx was lying or exaggerating. His words were blaring honesty, fear, amazement, gratitude, and most of all… concern about my future. Plainly said, my father, Lennox Gentry, was biologically half the mystical creature I had adored almost half of my life.
He pulled my wet shirt over my head and tossed it in a white plastic basket. “The whole ‘siren’ thing isn’t a myth either. She will call for you.”

“Kid, listen to me. I won’t ever let you go. Whatever you need from me, or whoever you need me to be,” he rattled my hand to hold my attention that was already glued to him, “I have it in me to be it. Understand?” His jaw locked and his brown eyes watered. “I stayed by your dad’s side until I couldn’t in order to save his life. Your life.”

It was my tenth Life Date, AKA birthday, and I was on the back of Dad’s bike for the first time on a ride with his club members. I squinted, hearing the bullets ring through the air, all over again, and my dad calling out to me before he fell to the unforgiving earth.
“I don’t know,” he was trembling, “but the last time I heard that shriek… my mermaid died.”

Still running in slow motion, I acknowledged how life can’t grow without the sun. That was her pain. My rejection, to her, was interpreted as losing me—was like losing the sun—her life. I had felt this earlier, but now the realization was so clear: I would never deny her anything, ever again.

Seeing the edge of the seawall, I didn’t slow my steps. Urgency pushed me forward. My heart denied gravity, and I leaped into the dark sky, pushing off the wall. My arms and legs kept moving, just like the day I should’ve died on my tenth Life Date. I was reliving it, falling, this time willingly, and all while roaring, “Saleeniiiii!”
If it is possible to sigh underwater, that is what I did. I felt the shift inside my body. A realization clicked into place. Saleeni was no family member. She was… is… my destiny.

As she leaned in, my gut tightened with a hunger not even beautiful Tallulah had me feeling. Panting heavily, I did my best to be a gentleman. “But you don’t even know my—” I’d meant to say name, but as soon as her open mouth hung only a breath from mine and her tongue crossed the barrier, I was lost. Unleashed. My eyes closed, and I moaned through the fever she was causing. My own tongue reached to touch hers.

I gawked. “My knuckles.” I didn’t even know I’d lost them. They had been in my pocket during the travels. “How’d you find—” I stopped talking when she took my right damaged hand and placed the brass onto my fingers.
I cringed when Saleeni kissed my ugly nub of a digit, thinking she must pity me, but that changed when she brought us back face to face, smiling. “Mad. G.”

Each of us wrapped the other in an embrace that was like a shield of love, something I had never encountered. The emotions were thick and blended with a natural way of life, combining with a spirit-to-spirit connection. Naked breast pressed against my bare chest as wild fury built between us. Her head lolled back, and the moonlight found her neck, as if to lure my lips forward.

The inner guilt I felt was enough to fill me with shame. “Jesus, I’m so sorry.” I had a raging hard-on, so ready for sex. And I didn’t even know if sex was possible with a mermaid not in more of a human form!

Abruptly, Saleeni left her post—me—and, with speed I’d never seen, was suddenly between Styx and me, shooting out of the water like a shark to shriek at him. She was no longer gorgeously glowing. Her whole body had gone menacingly dark and slick like an eel. Her breasts were covered with some sort of black, leathered scales.

She dared. A hand was suddenly twisted in my hair, yanking my head back and forcing my gaze to the sky. Then razor-sharp teeth slashed the right side of my chest. It stung but made my dick scream for more. I groaned as she continued her delicious attack.

Feeling out of my mind, yet spookily focused, I sensed it was now my turn. That’s when a pain in my upper jaw consumed me. My front teeth felt like they were rearranging, slowly. I went from an unimaginable sexual moment to one of intense pain and confusion. I tried to talk through the agony, “Sa-een—” but it was impossible. My mouth hung open, and blood began to drip out, the crimson droplets plopping into the ocean.

Everything that was happening no longer felt divine and mind-blowing with a side of sex appeal. Now it became alarming. I was floating in water, trying to fuck a mermaid even though I didn’t know how, my mouth dripping blood because my body was altering in some way. I had recently done what now felt like the unthinkable. I might have infected my friends with whatever I was becoming. No, no, no, no…

Mouth throbbing, I peered down and saw my fresh cuts had already closed. The lines where I had been bleeding, due to her teeth, were now black, like her skin had turned when angry at Styx for interfering… The symbol was like no artwork I’d ever seen. It was actually badass. I had been marked by her. The image looked ancient appearance, like something you would imagine on the wall of a cave from many centuries ago.

It felt as if the mattress I was lying on was opening up and trying to swallow me alive. In fear of being lost forever, my right hand shot into the air above me. In less than three days, I had been surrendered by my foster parents, picked up by a man who I was told was dead and ‘by the way I’m your grandpa’, brought to a new/old home, told my father was biologically part of some sort of aquatic race, and that my childhood imagination was actually factual.

His eyes started to water. “It means your dad got to be there—we got to be there for the most beautiful and saddest moment of his life. Just in time, he got to see his son be brought into this world.” He swallowed, a long and hard struggle. “And got to say goodbye to the only woman he would ever love.”

The planner in her took charge, and she asked me to marry her so that, legally, I could be responsible for the real Maddox Gentry. Make sure that after her death, if her false identity caught up to her—and you, legally, I would own what was once hers and give it to you. The real you.

“Smarty pants?” He gestured about. “Are we in kindergarten?” Then he explained, “I had no choice but to remove you from the household you cared about. You were about to get them all killed, acting like a rogue maniac, stalking that pastor of a church.”
Well fuck, silly rabbit. You have a shiny new pair of fangs.

He held me tight enough for me to understand this goodbye hurt him as deeply as it gutted me. I felt the stiffness of his muscles as his hands clutched me close. The sharp intake of breath. The tremble that seemed to take root inside him and flow into me. He said, 'I'll be okay. You stay strong. You hear me? You keep being a badass bitch and fight your way back to me.'

And then Ethan stepped forward, scooped me up, and took me from Gage with a determined set to his jaw. He hugged my body flush to his, and something about the gentle but firm hold finally reached into the frenzy of my mind. As I watched Johnny get in the nearby car, he angrily whispered, 'I swear to fuck we'll find him. I don't care how. We will. I swear it to you.'

A part of me felt so defeated. So battered and bruised by the reality that I was losing someone else that I loved. That, again, I had to say another goodbye I never saw coming so soon. Yes, we were foster kids with futures unwritten, but a part of me had believed we had built a little forever family. And it was killing me to let go of that dream. At a wicked speed, it was being snatched from me. First with Baby Blue. Then my Caleb. Now Johnny? All within a month?

A sob escaped as I buried my head in his neck. Sniffling against his warm skin, I hardly noticed that my face had pressed to the scarred section, or that he let me. Ethan wasn't obeying his steadfast rule: no touching what he considered a deformity—the damage from the fire that nearly took his life as a boy.

I believed him. Better yet, I felt his undeniable commitment to me. I even imagined hearing a whisper, 'Beloved,' something a young man would never say. That's how I knew it was from somewhere else or something else. Even in all my agony, I felt the presence of—Is that you, Baby Blue? I miss you so much! 'I'm going to crack wide open,' I warned, my lips so close to Ethan they touched his scarred skin.
Styx. A name Johnny knew and would cry for in his nightmares. Please be good to my friend.

My eyes finally opened. However, what I saw made me blink repeatedly. I thought my eyes were damaged from crying so much! It was the only explanation for seeing the luminous, lightly sparkling water washing over me and around me as if I were bathing in dancing stars.

I was already shaking my head. 'No way.' My fingers reached out, warmth flooding me again where I had felt cold after Johnny left. It was the water. The sparkles. They connected me to Johnny. 'I feel so close to him, Ethan. It's… wow.' I closed my eyes, and I could picture his face, his smile. 'It's like he's right here.'

'What does this mean for us? For Johnny? Is it only me and you, or will Gage, Finn, and Seb see water sparkling, too?' Ethan shook his head as if trying to clear it. 'What if this isn't the only thing that we see? What if we change in other ways?'
As I felt a pull to the water, to stick my hand back into the glittering spray that was now gone, I wondered if Johnny could feel me like I just felt him.

Disgusted, because her boyfriend recently died in a car wreck and she was already replacing him, I shook my head. 'Are you two serious right now? My only chance at revenge for Blue and the man who killed Caleb just rolled away in a stranger's car, and you two traitors are in here⁠—'

Johnny was gone! The son of a biker—a president at that—was my ace in the hole to see the pastor die. Johnny was the only one who could help me! And I needed it. That monster hurt her! He hurt my sweet baby Blue and took her away! The drunk driver took my friend! The fucking system took away Johnny, who was the first to truly make me feel I wasn't a pathetic stutterer!
She cried with me. 'I understand.' Her lip trembled. 'We both lost partners.'

Then, without an ounce of warning, I became so tired I could not keep my eyes open. I mumbled, 'Do you guys smell bleach?' I felt like I had spent all my energy truly punching someone to their final moments on this earth. It was eerie. 'Will you all stay with me?' Yet rewarding.
I was sitting in a tub full of fucking wet Tinker Bell dust. 'But… How…?'
Finally, Finn offered, 'If we guess something that's true,' he pointed, 'you pick a blue flower for Johnny. If we're wrong, pick a yellow one, meaning caution.'

Again, I racked my brain. Nightmares… Secrets… Name—I suddenly remembered the night we heard the new kid screaming. After his Noma's funeral. We ran up to his room in the attic. He was calling out for—'Styx.'

Finn shook as he reached out for one more blue flower. 'I don't want to push, but,' he took a deep breath, 'please tell me one more thing.' He held both flowers out for her to pick from. 'The-name-we're-not-to-say, is this man good for Johnny?' His voice cracked. 'I have to know.'
Head on Ethan's shoulder, she slowly reached out for the blue flower and laid it… vertically.

We never even admitted to being sore, having headaches, or aches from the accident. Caleb lost his life. What the fuck did we have to bitch about as far as injuries? Not that the Weathers could show up to a doctor or emergency room with five foster children who all sustained head injuries without authorities being involved. Nope, we would be separated and off to new homes.

I couldn't move. Nothing about a new ride could spur me into joy. The reason we needed it was far too tragic. But for the lovable foster parents who refused to give up on us, I numbly named it: 'Indestructible Tonka.'

Luckily, Dale and Harmony gave us the time we asked for. The next whole day we slept, all having dreams of peculiar things like streetlights, traffic signs, dashboard lights, the smell of bleach, fast food meals, and growing legs that kept wanting to cramp up due to being stuck in a car for too long. And a cloaked man, but all we could see was his grey goatee blowing in the wind that didn't exist.

From some sort of bridge I'd never seen, I'd been falling toward water, but in slow motion. On the way down, the same figure, with a grey goatee, in a dark cloak, was standing in a wooden John boat, rowing his way past where I was going to land. As he disappeared into a mist to my left, I crashed into an ocean.
As I shut the door, he mumbled, 'Zero-four-nine-nine.' Huh?
My scars weren't only skin deep… and this young woman knew it. Her cool touch on my scarred face; she whispered, 'You will never convince me her death is your fault.'
She folded into her lap, sobbing. 'Ethan, what if he wants to call home?' She hit the bed with a little fist. 'I know it's crazy, but I can feel him wanting to call home.'
Next thing I knew, I was on my back, my PJ T-shirt in her fists. 'I've waited so long for this. Why can't you see that?'

But her gasp, an inkling of her feeling pain, had an instant guilt taking over. From under me, she grabbed her mouth, wincing in pain. Oh no! 'Sarah—' But then the same relentless physical pain crashed into me. Oh fuck! I grabbed my mouth and fell over and rolled off her bed.

She reached for me as I crawled away. She even followed me out the door as we stumbled to our feet. I was shocked to bump into Gage, who was, unbelievably, also holding his mouth. Next to him were Finn and Sebastian. All holding their mouths.

He pointed to the water. 'Is it she who is triggering your difference? Compared to your dad?' Unexpectedly, his smile faded and was replaced by an expression that I would guess to be full of regret. He quietly said, 'He didn't fall in love with a mermaid.'
'Even the moon,' he explained. 'We say full moon, new moon, crescent… all the same fucking moon. Just different phases.' He gazed at me as if waiting for something.

With no other boats around, hence no one to help me, and us being a good distance from shore, this dude's upper body just floated above the water. He was noooo beauty like the mermaid I had been with. He was… His energy… Well, I reached for my gun at my back.

'He reached out for my boy, Maddox. I didn't know what he was going to do!' He ran his strong hand over his face again, this time smearing tears. 'I couldn't help it.' He gasped, lost in his own story. 'I suddenly had a knife in my hand and stabbed his arm.'

I don't know how to explain it, but I instantly knew I had made a huge mistake. It flowed through me like a wave of unknown knowledge. Something I should've known all along but didn't—a hindrance of being human. An out-of-body experience.

'Glittery blue blood dripped into the boat. I swear every star in his blood was… alive. Knowledge. Lessons. The divine.' He struggled to breathe again, his voice cracking like an earthquake rattling the ground we live upon. 'I dropped the knife because it felt as if I had just stabbed… a-a-a god of some sort.'
The stories, the myths about these mermaid creatures got it all wrong. They are not big fish that can talk or walk. Maddox, they are something… so much more.
Eyes full of tears that glittered to me like the blood he was describing, he nodded. Then, without looking away from me, he pointed to the water in front of us. 'As is she.'
Oh my God, this kiss. It was a seal of all our unspoken promises. It was the oath of joining life forces.

I was unaware that Saleeni and I, connected spiritually and physically, had risen from the water until I heard Styx crying. I pulled my mouth from Saleeni's to see him still on the wall, but now standing. The bliss on his face appeared as if he felt complete—had fulfilled a promise of his own. Raw in feelings, he said, 'You two are beautiful together.' Then he waved before walking away to the clubhouse.
'From what Noma told me, you seemed to sense Saleeni all the way to Cali. Imagine what she senses with you so close.'

'I came across a book on Greek mythology.' Like a mouse in a lab trying to pass a course for a piece of cheese, my mind continued to search for connections. The book had read things like… Journey to the underworld… Price to be paid… 'The river, the water, binding together souls with divine oaths—' I peered up at Styx on the stool. 'Oh shit.'
My lungs threatened to seize. 'The clubhouse on a peninsula. One way in. One way out.'

'My mermaid, Lennox's mother, her name was River. Well, that is the English version and much easier to pronounce. That's what I learned that day on the boat. Also explained was that my son was to take her place, guarding the boundary between two different worlds.'

Well, I had over a decade before the 'catch' was to be cashed in. Lennox was to impregnate another mermaid.' He held up a hand to stop me. 'Sounds creepy to guarantee your son's future 'prospects', but it was that or he, a little boy, be dragged underwater to, well, I'm not sure, to be honest. I had to buy us time to figure a way out of this mess.'

At a young age, Lennox fell in love with your mama. Absolutely refused when his time had come to 'do the deed'.' Holding a beer, his arm hung at his side as if too heavy to lift. 'That love, so pure and true, cost us dearly. It would start an avalanche of consequences.'
Life Date. My jaw hung. 'I turned ten the day he died.'
Sitting forward, hoping it would help me breathe, I mumbled, 'I was 'exiled' for eight years.'
'Kind of balanced out, right?' He started pacing again. 'Also? It is written that the River Styx carries the power to grant properties. River died giving birth to Lennox, so in came a job for me.'

'Why did River give Dad, an infant needed in the underworld, to you?' I shrugged, not wanting to sound stupid or ask a question he already had an answer for, but… 'Instead of her own kind? Had she not, you wouldn't even know he was alive, right?'
Styx's lips vibrated off each other like a motorboat as he blew out air, his eyes filling with doubt. 'I assumed the birth.'

'He wanted you to know the truth. He wished I had told him sooner than I did.' His chest heaved for a couple of seconds before he told me, 'He was going to tell you…' His voice cracked, 'On your tenth birthday.'
'Lennox called it The Lagoon. Happy late Life Date, Baby Boy.'

I jerked to a stop when I saw a very long underground tunnel, about four feet wide and tall. It pointed directly under my room, yet I couldn't see the end of it. 'Wait a minute. Does this lead to the ocean?'

'I promised not to lie to you. So, that answer is I don't know for sure how, but she has stayed alive for all these years you were gone.' He dared a grin. 'And from what I've seen since you've been back, you are the one in danger.'
My mouth gaped as my air was robbed from me. I barely had enough to say, 'Misfits.'
Like a bull sure to keep a testosterone-riddled elephant in check, this man roared back, 'To protect the gates!'
His whole form exhaled, from exhaustion and possibly also confusion of his own, but his answer felt as if he believed it. 'No. I think you're the Boundary.'

'But after the cut to the arm, I felt all of this knowledge.' His hands raised to either side of his head, then began to widen. 'My perception changed, so epically, it was as if I gained fifty more sets of eyes. For a short amount of time, I was able to see all around me at once. And all that was around me was nothing I had ever thought everything to be.'
'The blindness is the façade. The worry over trivial matters is the trickery. It is the pathway of the truth.' He pointed to me again.
'I am the mother fucking storm, asshole.' I headed to the freezer for nuclear food.

As soon as my eyes open, they begin to water and burn, not wanting to stay open. I'm on the living room floor, right where I had been fighting him. I don't remember the last hit that knocked me out, but my head hurts so bad I'm sure he used a bat or board of some sort.
My brain struggles to understand what my eyes are showing me as I scan up to see my little sister, hanging by her hair. Little arms extend out to me while she screams in pain.

I sit up in bed, sweating as if I had truly been in that fire. Grabbing my chest, I did my best to convince my lungs they weren't full of smoke. Oh, Ethan. My poor friend. I'm so sorry. The kitchen scene with Blue's oven mitt on fire now made so much sense. And Harmony's written words: He had a sister.…
I was swimming, exploring, when I was called by my mother. She had been with my family, at a distance from me, inspecting pillars of a bridge the humans used.

'The shared dream was the day of the accident with Dad. Saleeni was with her family. They were agitated, but she was too young to notice, so she didn't stay close to them.' I swallowed. 'It's what saved her.'
I drew in air to speak of that horrid day. 'From the bomb attached to a bridge's pillar.'
Styx was paler than I had ever seen him. 'Because they didn't plant it.' He stumbled back a few steps. 'That bomb wasn't for us.'

He was the one who insisted I go to counseling because some cruelties had ways of digging deep and forming barbs that were hard to yank free. I would always appreciate his intervention. At the time, I had been angry, but maturity and time had shown me that Dale acted with a pure heart and with the best intentions. He just never knew that the foster kid he lost to suicide had also been my first consensual lover.
'And to me, you'll always be my son.'
Wham! That's what the truth felt like to my stomach. A gut punch, reminding me that my failure had been right there all along. Ever since I got Caleb killed.
He rocked me. 'It was the drunk driver's fault.' He whispered in my ear, 'That's why I'm not sorry the asshole is dead.'
I suddenly remembered Sarah, in the car the night Blue died. She sneered. 'You cross lines in your sleep.' She declared, 'I've held your hand while you check off your 'revenge list'.'

'I said beat, didn't I?' Dale held up two fists. The ones he taught us how to spar with and protect ourselves with. 'I talked to a buddy at the precinct. There was too much bleach to get any DNA, but no weapon was involved according to the coroner.'
'An innocent child was found in a field nearby our church. A godly place! I'm devastated. Our entire community has been shocked by this young girl's death.'
Taking a deep breath, thinking of precious Blue, I knew I could kill for her. However, as Dale warned, I couldn't let my fellow fosters go down for it.
Shockingly, the only one seeming to have doubts like me was Sarah. Her hands wrung, over and over. 'Don't you all feel like we have something else to be doing right now?'
Er… I shook my head, praying he could hear me. 'No. Seb. No sea. She's in Heaven's gracious hands now.'
Tightening my hold, I vowed, 'I will. Just be smart about it. Let's keep Dale off our course, and let's be sure we don't get caught.'
The old Sebastian faded away as a livid man took his place once again. 'And I get to do it.'
I hope you forgive me for taking that from you.
I was mortified! I even threw Ethan to his back and crawled on top of him like an animal!
I thought I loved him… Now, I realize he was even more fucked up than me.
Finn now pressed it against my own chest. 'In here is so deep and precious.' He smiled, but the gesture was full of pain. 'You give beyond your means.'

Until that day, I had never sobbed with such truth. Every cry had been strangled before this day. Every cry had been ripped from my shattered heart. That's why this cry was so different. It poured out of me like a river that had been begging for years to be freed.
Finn didn't need an explanation for the tears flowing from me. He only squeezed my hand and said, 'Girl, you and I are, indefinitely, anchored to our storms.'

Finn smiled at me. I couldn't be sure; however, I sensed in his smile that he was proud I had just caught on to this amazing reveal, and he was the one who got to show it to me. 'Like you are the star of his water.'
'But, Kristen, you already made the choice to help with Caleb and Blue. What does it matter now if you help us talk to Johnny?'

'I've always known my actions could lead to prison one day.' She paused, her chin lifting as our eyes met. 'But I still chose to help. I'm still choosing, Sarah. And you need to realize that sometimes my silence, my withholding information… is protection.'

'See, that's how naïve you are. You are clueless about how to handle all this. That's a name I've never heard until now.' She chided, 'Johnny's family has been doing all they can to shield him from leaving any trails, yet you dare to open a possibly dangerous one.'
As if all energy had been drained from her, she tapped on her phone. The name River was all I could see.

My spinning mind raced me back to the night Blue died. When we were riding in Bertha, Sebastian insisted Johnny be real with us. In return, Johnny had yelled, 'All of you being beaten to death to get info on me!'
From the driver's seat, Finn unbuckled me, and Ethan scooped me into his arms. 'Memories haunting you, baby.'
I assumed he was referring to Caleb, Blue, and Johnny, but when he carried me into the house past worried faces and someone whispering 'anniversary', I remembered what day it was.

She never did when this happened to her. During nightmares, or times like this when she became catatonic from the trauma in her past, she was unable to move a muscle to prevent the memories of horrors inflicted on her. I still didn't know every detail, but over the years, we'd learned enough. Learned that bad shit had happened to her when she was in elementary school. The kind of fucked up bullshit even the news media hesitated to cover.

The saddest tears fell from Seb's eyes onto the stair below. 'A part of me left with her when she died.' He was quiet, adding, 'I felt it. For a precious moment, I got to be closer to her than ever before. Then…'
'Please don't be mad at me for looking forward to the day I die.'
'Then I'll look forward to every horrible dream.'
'It was my father, Ethan. He was the one with the gun.'

'Then he just turned around and left. When the police came to the school, I heard them whispering. The shooter had gone home and killed his wife, then himself.' She hiccupped a cry. 'I guess beating her was no longer enough.'
'What a pair we make. Both with fathers who tried to kill us. Both with fathers who succeeded with our mothers.'
'My research has stumped me. Lots of questions. I've found claims from previous followers that report medical care is against the religion.'

How am I not going to kill him right in front of Dale and Harmony? I peered around the van. All Misfits' eyes were locked on him like the Sinners we had become. How am I going to keep any of us from killing him? As soon as this pastor spewed false sorrow, he was as good as dead.
Ethan slid the portrait under his robe as if there was nothing to see. To Seb, he whispered, 'I got your girl. Now chill.'
Four angry penises were whipped out and happily pissed all over the car we were sure Blue's donations were paying for. Hell, I hit the handle, so he'd have to touch it when he opened the door.
'Soon, motherfucker. Soon, you're done hurting the innocent.'

There, floating toward heaven and our angel, were dozens of glowing paper lanterns. The higher they went, the wider the gap between them grew. As the wind caught and lifted the lights higher, the sky filled with flickering pops of color against the darkness. And to further announce the beauty and serenity of the moment, the stars appeared and twinkled in between those fairy-like lights.
It's like she was there with us. A shroud of warmth that can only be described as a ghostly embrace. The feeling stayed with me until the lights disappeared.

Because we couldn't get concrete to harden once submerged in water, the last part of the tunnel would be a pre-fabricated concrete tube, slightly smaller than the tunnel so it could slide in. On one end, there was metal, like the end of the tunnel, so we could weld them together like an underwater oil pipe.

The kiss was to be short and sweet, but my hands suddenly seized the back of her head and neck and refused to let her go. She hung in the air as my tongue possessed her mouth, so fucking hungry for more.

As if I were now the siren, her arms floated to her sides in surrender, letting me fully support her. An impossibility for a human who would have ended up with a broken neck. For a magical being? It was sensational. We drank in each other's desires, desperate for the day we could see them through to a whole new level.
Her eyes drifted back shut, and her proud smile said, 'Stronger.' I suddenly understood I had controlled her speed.

We even strapped two handheld mini air tanks to each of us for when we reached the water. We weren't sure of the physics. Styx was concerned the pressure of the water wouldn't create a slow enough leak. And because he was extra paranoid now, he refused to use the internet or search Google on his cell phone for answers.

The pressure of all the water weight was so intense, circling us as if it was being shot in from below by a fire hose. Our bodies now drifted out of control, at the mercy of the rush of seawater pushing under and around us through the tunnel.

Green? I dared to look behind me. There she was, my beautiful siren, eyes beaming, gaining on us. Moving through and past two out-of-control bodies, I felt her grab my hand. My arm almost dislocated during the initial pull, but I was thrilled to see Styx being dragged with me. A tail propelled us up through the tunnel built for its owner.

That moment never came. Not in the form I had imagined. I had expected this epic union; Saleeni rushing to be in my arms. Instead, only her eyes showing above the water, she circled in place, studying everything around her.

All I had wanted to do was to protect her, but now, trying to view all this—the lagoon, surrounding walls, no windows—from innocent non-human eyes, I realized I had imprisoned her, literally, in a concrete pool.
I lifted the gate. I love you, Saleeni.
My jaw locked, and I repeated words. I am the motherfucking storm. Then I threw the gate.
I swear to God, I could've cried the happiest of tears. Laughter was melting away fear, and hope was blooming.
'I need skylights for her.' Blindly, I pointed up in the air with my free hand. 'Up there.'
Would've loved to have her on the back of my bike someday.' My throat tightened. 'Hate that my Old Lady has to stay hidden.' I shrugged. 'I'm proud of her.'

A couple of days after Blue's vigil, all of us Misfits were sprawled on the couch watching TV when Dale came running down the stairs. I sat up when I saw the horror on his face as he scanned all of us. Then he sighed so heavily he had to rest his hands on his knees. 'You're all safe.'
When my blood oath palm began to itch, I remembered Johnny's sliding mirror.

Then I snuck to my room, grabbed a book, jumped into bed, and faked reading. As soon as I heard Dale talking and coming up the stairs, I realized my book was upside down. Shit! I fixed it just in time.
Finn's nostril flared as he stared at Dale, almost as if wondering how many nerves to stomp on. Then he replied, 'Because he is the son of the president of a deadly biker club.'
'Goddamnit. He always jumped when he heard a bike.'
Finn squinted. His neck strained. Then he growled, 'Her father.'
'Don't take a life. Don't be like that bastard of a man.' She sobbed, 'Be the beautiful soul you are.'
'If anything ever happens in this house, biker-related or whoever, don't try to save me or Dale. Get to John—Finn's room. Pull that mirror over the door. Hide away. Got it?'
Religious or not, when someone believes they are righteous, their actions to defend their beliefs can become… deadly. That made both the pastor and me anchored to our horrific storm.
I, without knowing it, had been a part of teaching Blue to say… no.
He watched the ball as he dribbled it back up the driveway. Making a shot, he said, 'That's why I got a gun.'
'Once you draw your weapon, the playing field changes, and all around you are now in the game.'
'Crash. Destiny. One and the same, in your case.' He exhaled. 'Glad you got the HOG back. It's another gift from your dad.'
The holster was slick, dark brown leather. Engraved in the leather that went around my left arm and near my heart was the phrase Boundary of the Underworld.
Foreign voices in foreign languages entered my mind. Some were happy, some were scared… Then feelings, not mine but the feelings of others, entered my spirit… I sighed. 'Water holds memories.'
Saleeni leaned her head to mine. 'B-Blood and… h-heart.'

In the glow of the pool's blue lighting, Saleeni was wearing some sort of seaweed crown. It was adorable on her, though somewhat creepy, decorated with pearls and odd human things like an old tiny fishing hook, a key, and an earring.
She gasped. Then I felt… I love you also.
Time slowed as her mouth hovered in front of mine, touching me with only a breath. I swear it was delivering something to my tongue. Every molecule landed with the faintest pop.

Imagine being at the altar of your own wedding, and as soon as you and your significant other exchanged the words 'I do,' you no longer had one secret from each other. Not one dark corner of your mind remained hidden.

It was as if we were becoming each other's anchor, preparing to ground one another through any storm we must face. Together, we would find the strength, the balance, and the patience to survive it all.
'L-Love,' she whispered for the very first time.
Saleeni rested on top of me, also spent and breathless. 'I love you, Maddox.'
My mermaid… now had legs.
Then, I heard the bellow of a human father screaming out for his son. 'Maaaaddoooooox!'

A splash in the water had me swimming as fast as I could, hoping there was something to salvage. That is when I saw the precious boy, injured, reaching out for the yellow material Lennox wore when on his two-wheeled vehicle. When he did this, my family's blood recognized him and rushed to his wound, wanting to bind with him so they could communicate with my youth. But everything we were is what caused the explosion…
Tears dripped down my face as I realized the connection. Every person whom Johnny blessed with a blood oath was literally the same. All without blood family, all at the mercy of destiny.
My knees buckled at his grave. 'Caleb,' I cried, my hands catching me before I crumbled fully. 'We're still connected.' In gratitude, I clutched my hands together at my chest. 'I feel you now.'

'All those innocents he invited online and during his interview. The bastard is preparing for new members for his church… and their children.' A violent urge to throw up had me bending over, placing my hands on my knees.

I swam for days and days, only stopping to eat and rest for very short periods of time. I faced sharks, huge ships, and things I had never seen before. I fought currents. I was caught in a net with sea creatures who were so scared. I escaped. I learned. I survived until finally reaching a coast close to the boy who no longer felt as young as he once was.
My tears fell to his arm I wouldn't let go of. 'And felt what she felt.' I wept. 'Us, I saw us from the water.'
'When our mouths hurt, we yelled it. 'Mad G'. It stands for Maddox Gentry.'
Even though I was begging, wanton-like, my true self wanted to be fully present the first time Ethan and I had sex.
'I've never been so turned on in my life.' I heard a bump as if he fell into my dresser. 'I have to go take a shower.'
'Went for the pastor. I gotta go get them.'
Those fucking traitorous choir boy wannabes! I jumped to my feet and ran to the closet.
I'm coming for you fuckers!

As a mermaid, Saleeni was voluptuous. Absolutely riveting and fierce. In human form, she was pixie-like. Her long fin had transformed into petite legs and little feet that didn't reach my ankles when she rested her head on my shoulder. Instantly, I recognized how vulnerable she was. Her human form was way more fragile than her mystical one.

How I managed to mark her as she had done me, with some sort of ancient symbol, was beyond comprehension. I hadn't maneuvered my fangs to create some design on her skin. I just held on with a vengeance I was feeling guilty about.
'Uh, okay.' I sat down and got to work. One folder read Maddox Gentry and the other Johnny Watts.
'Your fangs. They started to grow again but retreated when you put those on.' He nodded. 'Helps you maintain some self-control.'

'According to what Saleeni said in the water when you got super-hot to the touch, and the alpha energy that pours off you when you get angry… Yeah, I think we got more to come.' He sat back in the President chair. 'Hopefully, Saleeni will have some answers.'
'Some didn't turn human well. Brittle bones shattered. They screamed in pain.'
'Part of the transformation. River Styx helped me pass over safely.'

Naked, her long hair covering her breasts, she kissed me, then walked into the pool. Sinking into the water, facing me, her delicate fingers started to rub the scar I gave her. Her eyes fluttered shut. The blue lights in the pool let me watch the transition. Her legs began to blur. The blur grew into an esoteric moving fog. Then, what formed was her long tail and lovely transparent fin.
The Misfits were setting a fire that might burn away the last innocence in their damaged hearts. I couldn't let that happen. I needed to be the one to send the pastor to Hell.
'We know. Did you think you were out here all those years, unprotected at the Weathers'?' He pointed to one of his cut's patches. 'That's how we are now the Saltbone Sinners.'
It was my very own cut. My rank patch read: Someday President

I heard Styx cursing behind me, but I had to break my promise to him. I now knew who I had to save. Pulling down my full ski mask, I ran faster than I ever had because the pastor had her in his sights. And a rifle pointed at her chest.

Carrying a weapon had been so brand new to me. Under such immense fear, I didn't even think to retrieve it and reacted on natural instincts. Like I had done in the water with Saleeni, time slowed. I manipulated seconds so I could beat the slug shot that had been fired. As I had from the seawall, I let my body soar like an athlete so I could be my dear friend's shield.
When the buckshot slammed into my back, I knew I had succeeded.

Like illegal dogfighting, my father fought me. For years, I was forced into confinement to fight another innocent. Some kids pissed themselves and cried. Some were already soulless, far from the kind child they'd been born to be.

Back then, every time I lifted my fists to survive another day, it felt like another piece of any hope I had left was eaten away. But not fighting would cost me. Dad was brutally cruel with his 'motivations'. He even forced me to beat… I can't talk about what I was forced to do to Sam.

Once Dad finally got busted over his criminal ring of abuse, and I was taken away, I promised myself I would never be controlled again. That's why I swung like mad when a body collided with mine, and I was tackled to the ground.

We both froze when a gun fired into the night. From the ground, we peered in the direction the sound had come from. What I saw was confusing. Even though it was all happening so fast, time slowed. Something began to shift inside me. It was hard to describe, but it felt like an invisible force wrapped a blanket around me. It wasn't restraining or threatening. It was actually… comforting, even though havoc and all hell were breaking loose around me.

As if high on drugs, I slowly reached out for this person's hand. As soon as I held it, I knew who this person was. I sighed because I had missed him so damn much. Then I leaned down to his ear and simply whispered, 'Brother, you don't need air to breathe.'
That was the craziest thing to say to someone, but just like that, brown eyes behind the ski mask shot open. He sharply inhaled. Then, selfless as always, Johnny asked, 'Is she okay?'
With an astonished smile, I looked to Sebastian. 'You just rescued Blue's sister.'

He ran a hand down his thick facial hair. 'Tonight, we found her bedroom hidden behind a fake wall. From what we can tell, by his clothes on the floor at her bed, he was in there with her when our shit-storm hit.'
'The furniture in that room… older, dated, dusty. The little one isn't the first, if you catch my drift.'

Feeling ill, I looked to the tiny girl who appeared to be barely six. She looked spooked and was holding Sarah's hand. How long had she been hidden away? Her whole life? Had Blue been trapped in that hidden room also? How young was Blue when the pastor started abusing our friend? Oh, Blue.

One foot in the van, one still on the ground, Seb observed where his revenge lay, served on a platter for the taking. Then he looked to the little girl. His eyes shifting back to the bearded man, he smirked. 'Amazing how fast focus can change.'
'Listen up.' Another man handed Finn fifty bucks. 'For now, act normal. Go to McDonald's, clean them out of cheeseburgers, then get your asses home.'
With the Jeep now squealing its tires, he said, 'Johnny being who he is now makes a whole lot more sense. I think they're his people.'
She held us. 'My boys. You can do no wrong in my eyes. And I already have hot chocolate on the stove.'

In the kitchen were Dale, Sebastian, Sarah, Kristen, and the little girl eating ice cream. Already bathed and wearing one of Sarah's pajamas that drowned her, she was sitting on the island's countertop, being smiled at as if she were a zoo's favorite attraction.

That connection, the one I counted on, rose to a whole new level. Still with arms locked together, now bent and putting us chest to chest, we were both standing but not touching the ground. We were moving but not by our feet. It was more like a mystical, invisible conveyor belt.
He kept blinking. 'It's… You… Kid, your skin is like black leather. Saleeni did this when she was mad at me. Remember?'

I glanced out the back window to see my friends, not sure when I would see them again, and was gifted with words from Seb. He chose to protect over murder. The young man I saw in the hospital, at Blue's side, had returned.

Disturbing Noma's gravesite would seem sacrilegious to some, I suppose, but leaving her behind was never going to happen. The alphas in Styx and I were going to have that woman near and under our care.
Cocky sat down after handing out bowls to fill. His chair squeaked under the pressure of a big man. 'Who the hell do you think taught her?'
Chewing through tears, I appreciated every pat on the back and shoulder. Most of all, I appreciated the kiss to the top of my head. 'The bravest. Our Baby Boy.'
'Jesus Christ.' Styx blew through a red light. 'They're in with the pastor.'

Two men had been stabbed in various places and tied to furniture. Another body lay on her side. No beautiful brown eyes to see. They were closed, but I knew it was her because of her greying blonde hair spread out behind her. I knew it was her because of who was holding her hand. And I knew she was dead because her blood had drained from the slice across her neck.
Three mothers. I had now lost three mothers. And I felt the blame for them all.
Dale was smiling. Blood dripped from his mouth. The courageous man was dying yet fucking smiling at me as if this wasn't all my fault. 'Your skin. You're made of dancing stars, Brass.'
He smiled again. 'Nothing is impossible, Brass.'
Inhaling, because she had forgotten to breathe until she felt me, she turned to my chest. 'Johnny.'
Remarkably, and impressively, their feet found stability. Then, these incredible beings stood taller, all letting me know they were ready.

With devastating tears and soft whispers, every foster paid their respects to our parents, then followed Maddox Gentry, with ultimate trust and more loyalty than one could ever deserve or demand. For it had to be given.
It was the flowers we had planted… Oh, my Caleb.
Opening my eyes, I took the last step forward and placed a hand on his left shoulder. I whispered, 'My turn to give you the time needed.'

Chills broke out over my whole body as I fully realized the young man named Johnny was gone. However, the admirable qualities that made his soul so rich, his heart so kind and giving, were beaming brightly. My friend was never going to be the same. He was now… ethereal.

Slowly and pitifully, Maddox turned in the chair, exposing a ghastly mutilated corpse behind him. The pastor had been stabbed so many times that his midsection no longer existed. He was now a shell. And I hoped he was in Hell.

As if the fatigue of killing someone so brutally had finally caught up to Maddox's human side, he barely rose from the chair before taking two faltering steps, then fell to his knees right in front of me. Magical blue eyes now brown again, he gazed up. 'I failed Dale and Harmony.'
'No.' With the weapon in one hand, blood and tissue dripping, I proudly wrapped my arms around Maddox. 'You don't know how to fail.'
'That you're still made of brass. A wonderful element, full of nature, strength, and the ability to survive anything.'

I found a washcloth and soap, then proceeded to clean his chest and stomach of the recently dried blood stuck to them. On his chest was a symbol I'd never seen before, in the form of a scar. When I gently scrubbed over it, removing blood, I felt a flutter in my stomach. This scar was no accident and had an otherworldly purpose.
Maddox grabbed my hand, then pulled it to his damp cheek. He sighed. 'Noma loved his music.'

'Listen, two cops will be found murdered. Two foster parents deceased. And five registered foster children MIA.' She sucked in air. 'This is huge. It means goodbye to a baseball scholarship. Goodbye to graduating high school. Goodbye to California. Goodbye to your identities, and hello to new ones and a magnitude of lies.'

'Baby Boy and I planned on taking his Noma home with us, but…' His lips pursed and moved, as this strong man fought not to cry. 'She will have to wait a little longer.' He coughed. 'Caleb is the one going home with Maddox.'
Then he finally admitted, 'Someday you will learn more, but 'Johnny' has had eyes on him since before he came to you years ago.'
Out in the water, the two embraced. They kissed, and they gave us hope. They gave us the strength for a goodbye we couldn't avoid any longer.

What would come next for us all was undetermined. Fate. Or maybe a little nudge from the River Styx and his ferry through the Underworld. But knowing we would someday be together again, that we'd reunite with our leader, was enough. We lifted our chins and were so very proud to be Sinners. Maddox's Saltbone Sinners. Because…
We are life… for each other.
